findings_qualitative.value: First detection of millimeter recombination line emission (H30alpha) toward the BN object.

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of mm RL emission toward the BN object.

findings_qualitative.value: H30alpha emission was not detected toward other radio sources in the field (source I and source n), largely due to line contamination from the Orion Hot Core.

evidence.quote: We also searched for H$30\alpha$ emission in the rest of the Orion BN/KL field, in particular from sources I and n, without success.

findings_qualitative.value: The millimeter RL arises from a dense, static base of the ionized envelope, whereas the centimeter line (H53alpha) traces an outflowing component.

evidence.quote: The mm RL appears to be arising from the dense ($N_e=8.4\times10^6$ cm$^{-3}$), static (bulk motions $<<10$ km s$^{-1}$) base of the ionized nebula around the central massive star in BN
Compared to the H$30\alpha$ line, the optically thicker H$53\alpha$ seems to trace gas outflowing toward us at $\sim 6.5$ km s$^{-1}$.

findings_qualitative.value: A significant fraction of the 1.3 mm continuum of BN may originate from line-of-sight dust emission.

evidence.quote: This suggests that dust contributes a significant fraction to the (sub)mm continuum of BN.

claims.hypothesis: Millimeter recombination lines can reliably determine the line-of-sight systemic velocity of the central star in BN.
claims.experiment: Observed the H30alpha line at 231.9 GHz with ALMA SV data, filtering short baselines to remove extended hot-core sidelobes, and compared its profile with the VLA H53alpha line.
claims.result: H30alpha is detected with v_LSR = 26.3 +/- 0.5 km s^-1 and FWHM = 15.4 +/- 1.3 km s^-1, narrower than H53alpha and redshifted by ~6.5 km s^-1.
claims.finding: Because H30alpha is optically thinner and unaffected by pressure broadening, it provides the systemic line-of-sight velocity of BN as v_LSR = 26.3 km s^-1.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the H$30\alpha$ line should give a better estimation of the line-of-sight velocity of the star inside the BN nebula, $v_\mathrm{LSR}\mathrm{(BN)}=26.3\pm0.5$ km s$^{-1}$.

claims.hypothesis: The ionized gas around BN is characterized by high electron density, low electron temperature, and quiescent base kinematics.
claims.experiment: Decomposed the H30alpha and H53alpha linewidths and intensity ratios into thermal, pressure, and dynamical components using standard recombination line formulas.
claims.result: The narrow H30alpha linewidth constrains Te < 4900 K and dynamical bulk motions << 10 km s^-1, while H53alpha broadening yields an average electron density Ne = 8.4 x 10^6 cm^-3.
claims.finding: The mm recombination line arises from the dense, gravitationally confined base of the ionized envelope around the central ~10 M_sun star.

evidence.quote: Therefore, for the gas traced by the H30$\alpha$ line, $T_e$ is at most 4900 K, and the bulk gas motions are constrained to be much smaller than the thermal width. Finally, using equation 3 of (cite: kzk08), the average electron density traced by these RLs is $N_e=8.4\times10^6$ cm$^{-3}$.

claims.hypothesis: The Becklin-Neugebauer object is variable in the millimeter continuum.
claims.experiment: Compared the ALMA 1.3 mm flux density (126 +/- 14 mJy) with historical OVRO (150 +/- 50 mJy) and CARMA (< 34 mJy) measurements, alongside multi-epoch VLA 8.4 GHz continuum data.
claims.result: While the 8.4 GHz cm flux is stable within 30%, the CARMA non-detection differs significantly from ALMA and OVRO detections.
claims.finding: BN may exhibit large millimeter flux variations, but systematic errors in mm calibration and inhomogeneous u-v coverages preclude a definitive conclusion without uniform monitoring.

evidence.quote: It is possible that BN is variable in the (sub)mm continuum. While our detection of BN is consistent with the 218 GHz flux of $S=150\pm50$ mJy (from OVRO observations in 1993 and 1994) reported by (cite: plambeck95) and (cite: blake96), (cite: fs08) do not detect BN at 231 GHz down to a $3\sigma$ level of $\sim 34$ mJy (CARMA observations in 2007). However, the significance of these variations can be affected by the inhomogeneity of the mm observations.

why_this_data.value: Millimeter recombination lines are intrinsically brighter, more optically thin, and unaffected by pressure broadening compared to cm RLs, making ALMA Band 6 data uniquely suited to measure systemic velocity and physical conditions.

evidence.quote: Compared to their centimeter-wavelength counterparts, millimeter recombination lines (RLs) are intrinsically brighter and are free of pressure broadening.

why_this_method.value: Excluding short baselines (< 100 klambda) filters out the strong extended background and sidelobes from the nearby Orion Hot Core, isolating the compact emission from BN.

evidence.quote: We found that a minimum baseline length of $\approx 100$ k$\lambda$ gives optimal results, filtering out the emission on scales $>1\rlap.{''}4$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Imaging the hot core and Source I using restricted u-v coverage was rejected due to severe imaging artifacts/sidelobes.

evidence.quote: This degradation of the u-v coverage produces artifacts (closely-spaced sidelobes) close to source I and the HC, and we refrained from using this part of the image.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Imaging H30alpha without baseline restriction was considered, but sidelobes from blueshifted molecular lines near the HC contaminated the map.

evidence.quote: The H30$\alpha$ line is also detected in maps that use the complete baseline range, but bright molecular emission from the HC centered at $\sim 10$ MHz blueshifted with respect to the RL creates sidelobes that are for the most part removed by taking only the longest baselines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Standard electron temperature of Te = 10^4 K was rejected because pure thermal broadening would exceed the observed H30alpha linewidth.

evidence.quote: Also, in the BN object this line appears to be too narrow (15.4 km s$^{-1}$) even for pure thermal broadening at $T_e=10^4$ K (equation A.2).

how_they_decided_enough.value: Checked that the measured 1.3 mm flux density of BN remains consistent within 20% across different baseline filtering restrictions.

evidence.quote: We note that the flux density for BN is the same, within $20~\%$, regardless of the u-v coverage restriction applied.

limitations_admitted.value: Inhomogeneity and systematic calibration uncertainties in mm interferometry prevent proving mm continuum variability conclusively.

evidence.quote: However, the significance of these variations can be affected by the inhomogeneity of the mm observations.
We emphasize that only dedicated multiepoch observations with a uniform setup can clarify this issue.

limitations_admitted.value: H30alpha could not be detected toward Source I due to bright molecular line contamination from the nearby Hot Core.

evidence.quote: the proximity of source I to the HC contaminates any emission from the relatively faint RL with brighter, more extended molecular lines with rest frequencies within a few MHz of the H$30\alpha$ line.

limitations_admitted.value: The observed H30alpha to H53alpha line-to-continuum ratio is smaller than predicted for pure free-free emission (1.6 observed vs 6.4 expected), indicating substantial line-of-sight dust contamination in the 1.3 mm continuum.

evidence.quote: Under these assumptions, the expected ratio of the H30$\alpha$ to H$53\alpha$ line-to-continuum ratios is 6.4. However, the observed value is 1.6.

referee_caveats_inferred: Differences in u-v sampling and flux scale calibrations between CARMA and ALMA could account for the apparent millimeter flux differences rather than true intrinsic variability.
Potential non-LTE amplification or line-of-sight dust absorption could complicate simple LTE line-to-continuum interpretations.

reproducibility.score_reason: The raw and calibrated visibilities are publicly available from the ALMA SV archive, and the analysis uses standard CASA steps (uv-continuum subtraction, baseline filtering at >100 klambda, and Gaussian line fitting). Reproducing the exact flux and profile parameters within 10-20% is straightforward, though exact clean settings and channel intervals are omitted.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The dataset is public ALMA SV data (Orion BN/KL Band 6), and applying a 100 klambda baseline cutoff to inspect the H30alpha line profile and measure the BN 1.3 mm flux can directly verify the central claims and numeric values.
